text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: sustained p99 latency breach on pool-prod-us-west1-shared-gpu streaming endpoints. p95 260ms -> 480ms, p99 650ms -> 1.2s. Error budget nearing. Start triage.
Rohan (oncall): I'm looking. any deploys in last 10m?
deploy-bot: deploy finished by diego at 2026-03-15T18:41:10Z on pool-prod-us-west1-shared-gpu, image: runtime:v3.2.1
Maya (sre): seeing correlated spike in disk io wait on gpu nodes 21-24. iostat shows high await on nvme1.
Diego (runtime): hmm. quick check: are these streaming stalls or full requests timing out?
Maya (sre): streaming stalls. logs show many keepalive frames delayed, sessions stuck at chunk 3/5. sample session id s-3a7b.
Jun (custsuccess): flagged by customer support — Acme Analytics reported intermittent slow responses on realtime infer endpoint. they see p99 > 1s since ~18:40 UTC.
pm-elliot: please record customer impact: which customers and % of requests affected?
Maya (sre): rough traffic: pool handled 2.1k rps, about 3.4% of requests hit >1s at p99 window. Acme is high QPS but not the only one.
Rohan (oncall): OK initial hypothesis noisy neighbor causing IO contention on shared pool. Diego / Sophia, can we identify top tenants by IO?
Diego (runtime): running quick query on tenant stats.
Diego (runtime): output snippet:
```
tenant_id   cpu_ms   gpu_ms   blk_read_bytes   blk_write_bytes   active_sessions
tenant_acme  120000  340000  1.4GB            2.3GB              128
tenant_x7    50000   20000   12.1GB           18.3GB             96
tenant_zeta  30000   15000   100MB            80MB               12
```
Diego (runtime): tenant_x7 doing huge writes, suspecting checkpointing or dataset staging on worker disk.
Sophia (platform): which nodes host tenant_x7?
Diego (runtime): nodes gpu-21,gpu-22,gpu-23. nvme1 on those nodes shows sustained 200-350MB/s write.
Maya (sre): reproduction command used: ssh gpu-22 then `sudo iotop -aoP` shows processes under container runtime hitting high write.
Rohan (oncall): mitigation options: 1) throttle noisy tenant blkio, 2) migrate tenant to dedicated pool, 3) temporarily drain affected nodes and restart workers. prefer lowest customer impact.
Sophia (platform): can we apply cgroup blkio weight tweak live? we use containerd with cgroup v1/v2 mix. on gpu-22 we can set blkio.weight for the container to 100 from 1000 as emergency.
Diego (runtime): I can apply temporary throttle and also open a migration job to move tenant_x7 to tenant-dedicated-1. will take ~2-4m to start.
Rohan (oncall): do it. throttle first, then migrate. leave Acme on pool to avoid hurting their traffic.
Diego (runtime): running command:
```
# set blkio weight for container runtime id c12345
echo 100 > /sys/fs/cgroup/blkio/docker/c12345/blkio.weight
```
Diego (runtime): applied to the top noisy container on gpu-22 and gpu-21.
Maya (sre): monitoring: p99 dropped from 1.2s -> 420ms within 90s. p95 stable at ~300ms.
Jun (custsuccess): pinging Acme to confirm if they see improvement.
pm-elliot: note for timeline: throttle applied 18:44 UTC.
Jun (custsuccess): acme confirms measurable improvement; still occasional blips but much better.
Rohan (oncall): start migration now to dedicated pool. Diego, create migration task and apply sane QPS cap during move.
Diego (runtime): kicking migration job. using rolling stop/start for containers to preserve sessions. adding qps cap 50% during move.
deploy-bot: migration job started at 2026-03-15T18:46:31Z for tenant_x7 -> tenant-dedicated-1
Maya (sre): post-migration: gpu-23 shows io back to baseline, p99 180ms. overall pool p99 210ms.
Rohan (oncall): good. marking incident as mitigated for user-facing latency. still tracking root cause and possible timeout regressions in runtime.
Diego (runtime): initial root cause: tenant_x7 staged large model snapshots to local disk during live infer, causing heavy write amplification. runtime should enforce background i/o QoS for tenants.
Sophia (platform): action items: 1) enforce blkio weight defaults at sandbox creation, 2) add heuristic to detect heavy write storms and auto-isolate tenant, 3) add a migration playbook.
Maya (sre): monitoring follow-ups: add streaming stall alert rule on per-pool p99 > 800ms for 3m, and a separate IO await alert on nodes.
pm-elliot: we need customer comms: Jun to follow up with Acme and Diego to propose dedicated pool option if they need high throughput.
Jun (custsuccess): will draft an email and reach out with status and next steps.
Rohan (oncall): assigning owners for RCA: Diego runtime lead, Maya infra for monitoring, Sophia platform for prevention. I'll write timeline and severity.
Diego (runtime): quick note: deployment earlier by me v3.2.1 looked unrelated; it didn't change disk behavior. rollback not necessary.
Maya (sre): adding final metrics snapshot: pre-mitigation p99 1.2s, post-throttle p99 420ms, post-migration p99 180ms. incident start 18:40 UTC, mitigated 18:47 UTC.
Rohan (oncall): severity P2. will keep thread open for RCA notes. thanks all. :thumbsup:
